title: SAC: Disaggregated KV Cache System for Sparse Attention LLMs with CXL
event_hint: SAC system release: CXL-based disaggregated KV cache for sparse attention LLMs
problem: RDMA-based disaggregated KV cache systems perform full prefix cache fetching before decoding, causing transmission bottlenecks and local memory waste for sparse attention models where only a small fraction of KV entries are active
mechanism: CXL-based disaggregated memory with cache-line granularity load/store semantics enables on-demand fetching of only required top-k KV entries during inference

evidence.claim: SAC achieves 2.1x higher throughput compared to RDMA-based baselines
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-V3.2 model, SGLang framework, context lengths 16K-128K tokens

evidence.claim: SAC achieves 9.7x lower TTFT (Time to First Token) compared to RDMA-based baselines
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-V3.2 model, SGLang framework, context lengths 16K-128K tokens

evidence.claim: SAC achieves 1.8x lower TBT (Time Between Token) compared to RDMA-based baselines
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-V3.2 model, SGLang framework, context lengths 16K-128K tokens

evidence.claim: Only 21% of KV cache is actually utilized in 128K-context scenarios for DeepSeek-V3.2
evidence.condition: DeepSeek-V3.2, 128K context length, ShareGPT dataset with 1K-token output

evidence.claim: CXL-based disaggregated memory achieves 1.04-1.64x of local DRAM latency for sparse KV retrieval
evidence.condition: Sparse KV indices sampled from 128K-token context, DeepSeek-V3.2 MLA KV entry (512-dim latent + 64-dim RoPE, bfloat16)

evaluation_context: DeepSeek-V3.2 sparse attention model evaluated using SGLang framework across context lengths from 16K to 128K tokens; workload from ShareGPT dataset with 1K-token output; comparisons against RDMA-based disaggregated memory pool and non-disaggregated local memory upper bound
limitations: Evidence limited to abstract/introduction/motivation sections; detailed experimental methodology, hardware configurations, and complete evaluation results not reviewed; CXL memory access pattern results from microbenchmark (Figure 5) not end-to-end serving; specific CXL hardware generation (2.0/3.0) not specified; scalability beyond 128K context not addressed
project_relevance: Directly addresses memory semantics question by demonstrating how CXL's cache-line granularity load/store semantics enable fundamentally different disaggregated memory access patterns compared to RDMA's message-based send/recv model; shows 1.04-1.64x DRAM-equivalent latency for sparse access vs 4.0-19.7x for RDMA; validates CXL mem semantics for fine-grained, sparse KV access; DSA/IAA relevance indirect - work focuses on CXL fabric not CPU offload; end-to-end evidence from SGLang integration with 2.1x throughput, 9.7x TTFT, 1.8x TBT improvements

evidence_gaps.question: What are the exact hardware configurations for CXL memory, GPU instances, and RDMA network used in end-to-end evaluation?
What are the detailed baseline configurations for RDMA-based disaggregated systems being compared?
What are the complete experimental results including throughput, TTFT, TBT, and memory usage across different context lengths and concurrency levels?
